title: Medicine and Keeping Well
label: ch:ml-medicine
canDo: I can name medicine, treatment and cleanliness, and place them around the symptoms I can already say.

payoff.summary: From cold: three words around falling ill, and which one Malayalam did not have to borrow.
payoff.note: THE NOTE HELD ON ALL FIVE CHECKS, AND THIS TIME I RAN THE FIFTH ONE. 'The symptoms are taught (ML-A1-LEX-27) and nothing that treats them is' is a claim about EXISTING MATERIAL, which is the shape that caught me on ML-A1-TIME-09 one tranche ago -- a note that anticipates your check is making a claim, not reporting a result. So LEX-27's five probe atoms were opened rather than trusted, and ALL FIVE are named here because naming four of five is how a census starts drifting: viSappu (FEEL-01), kshiiNaM (-02), vEdana (-03), cuma (-04) and pani (-05) are all taught headwords in chapter 63. The claim is true. THE DOMAIN CHECK PAID OFF AGAIN AND IT SHAPES THE CHAPTER. vaidyan, the doctor, is taught at ML-C48-doctor (1310) -- so the learner has had the SYMPTOMS and the PERSON and nothing in between: no substance, no practice. That gap IS the chapter, and the chapter is built as a LINE: keep clean, fall ill, be treated, take the medicine. C48's OWN CAVEAT IS CARRIED FORWARD rather than tidied away: that lesson says vaidyan today usually points at a practitioner of the traditional medicine and that the hospital doctor goes by the English word, so ML-C107-chikitsa repeats it and marks its three-row table as ONE of the two pictures Kerala keeps side by side. THREE WORDS, CHOSEN BECAUSE THEY ARE THE LABEL'S THREE PARTS. marunnu, cikitsa and vRtti are medicine, treatment and hygiene, one word each. aashupatri (hospital) and guLika (tablet) were DROPPED, and the honest reason is that NEITHER IS IN THE LABEL -- not the script debt. The debt argument is weak and is not made: U+0D36 and U+0D33 are never-taught characters, but they already stand in 17 and 24 headwords respectively, so one more headword apiece would not have changed their standing. WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW IN THIS CHAPTER IS THE CLUSTER t+s. Every CODEPOINT in the three words is already script-taught and already in use in headwords, but ta-virama-sa is the corpus's FIRST occurrence of that conjunct in any headword, and ML-C107-chikitsa takes it apart rather than letting it pass as familiar. vRtti IS GLOSSED HONESTLY AS THE EVERYDAY WORD. It is cleanliness -- what you say about a room or a person's hands -- not hygiene as a subject, and the lesson says so outright rather than letting the exam label's English word stand unexamined. Its Sanskrit sense is CONDUCT, a way of living, and the road from conduct to cleanliness is offered as the traditional account rather than asserted, which is the treatment paLLikkooTaM got in chapter 103 after review caught the first draft asserting it. THE NATIVE/BORROWED SPLIT IS THE CHAPTER'S SECOND THREAD AND IT IS CHECKABLE, AND IT IS OFFERED AS A FACT ABOUT THESE THREE WORDS AND NOT AS A PATTERN: marunnu is Dravidian and Tamil has marundhu; cikitsa and vRtti are both Sanskrit. The chapter 103 school words are NOT the same shape and the first draft's claim that they were has been dropped -- paaThaM and pariiksha are Sanskrit, maarkku is English and paLLikkooTaM is a local compound, which is a story about INSTITUTIONS, not about a substance keeping its own name. THE THREE CEILING GREPS RUN IN DRAFT CAUGHT TWO CHAPTER NUMBERS in the recall before they reached the gate, and the full suite passed on the FIRST run for the third chapter running.
